source.title: Mechanism-Guided Selective Unlearning for RLVR-Induced Reasoning
source.authors: Chen-Yu Zhou; Qi-Liang Jiang; Shu-Ning Wu; Xuan-He Zhou

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests unlearning on RLVR checkpoints and argues that full-parameter gradient ascent has no clean operating point; its own results show a tradeoff between target forgetting and retained capability. It proposes MAST but does not test whether attacks recover unlearned knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning outcomes on mathematical-reasoning targets and retained benchmarks, so those results bear on version A. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompt changes; its mechanism diagnostics concern the SFT-to-RLVR update, not whether unlearning deletes knowledge or blocks access. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study unlearns RLVR-induced math reasoning on two Qwen models and reports target (MATH-forget) accuracy alongside retained utility (MATH-retain, GSM8K, MMLU) for GA, GA+retain, NPO, SimNPO and MAST. This bears on the 'targets near chance while keeping general ability' part of A, in a new setting (reasoning induced by RLVR rather than factual or hazardous knowledge). It runs no recovery attacks, so B–F are not tested. Classed T3 rather than T5: it does not argue that unlearning is shallow, it reports a new-setting forget/utility tradeoff.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors report MAST preserves broad capability (MMLU within 0.4 pp), and that its collateral advantage over full-parameter unlearning is statistically significant on both models.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies selective unlearning of RLVR-induced mathematical reasoning, not recovery attacks against the methods named in the claim. MAST ranks attention-projection tensors and restricts the update to a selected subset.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with learning rate and parameter-selection method; the paper also reports differences across model family and unlearning objective. At some higher strengths MAST incurs more collateral, while full-parameter GA collapses.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning lowers solution-trajectory log-probability while raising final-answer log-probability, for both MAST (−0.012/+0.078) and full GA (−0.143/+0.975).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forget accuracy and answer likelihood disagree after reasoning unlearning, so the answer string may stay likely while generated correctness falls.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code, configurations, manifests, and per-sample outputs are released, but gives no URL in the text)
record.problems: The evidence is limited to mathematical reasoning and two model families; strength is calibrated per model. The study does not test recovery attacks, and it does not state a chance-level reference for the target accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: The full strength frontiers in Section 4, Table 2 include additional settings not extracted here (primary MAST η = 7×10−6 and 1.5×10−5, primary full-parameter GA ≥ 1×10−5, Qwen3 MAST η = 1.5×10−5 and higher, and Qwen3 full-parameter GA ≥ 1.5×10−5). Table 5's detailed outcome rows for the retained MATH metric for NPO and SimNPO are included; other repeated descriptions of selected operating points are not duplicated. These omitted frontier points are additional strength settings or collapse outcomes; the selected and boundary settings above capture the reported tradeoff. No attack-recovery results are reported in the paper.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (relearning, prompting, quantization, ablation) recover the forgotten reasoning; no chance-level reference is stated for the free-response MATH forget split.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion; the mechanism diagnostics concern SFT-vs-RLVR updates.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery test.
MAST is a selective-unlearning method but is not tested against any recovery attack.

missing.what: Zero-shot MMLU (1000 examples) general-capability check: RLVR source 38.1%, MAST (GA) 37.7%, full GA 37.6%.
Base-model reference forget accuracy (Qwen2.5 base 34/150; Qwen3 base 31/150). This is the natural floor for removing RLVR-induced reasoning and is the only stated reference level.
Seed robustness of MAST forget counts: {37,37,41}/150 for GA and {41,39,39}/150 for NPO.

record.verdict_notes: The target is RLVR-induced math reasoning, not hazardous or factual knowledge, so the fit to the shallow-unlearning phenomenon is loose. The study speaks only to the efficacy/utility half of version A and never tests recovery. The original sources (WMDP etc.) are cited but this is not one of them. Row-state convention is mixed: forget rows mark forgetting achieved, while retain/GSM8K rows mark utility kept; several retain/GSM8K states were inconsistent with the size of the drops and are corrected above. MAST's selected point (37/150) lands close to the base model (34/150), which is arguably near-complete removal of the RLVR increment, but the paper does not frame it that way.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests target forgetting and retained performance, but not whether attacks recover the target knowledge. It does not establish a chance-level reference for MATH accuracy.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation to recover the target; the mechanism analysis does not test whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery test.
MAST is proposed as a selective unlearning method, but resistance to the listed recovery attacks is not tested or reported.

relationships.condition: MAST (GA/NPO/SimNPO) on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and Qwen3-1.7B-Base RLVR checkpoints
relationships.reason: Utility is kept but forgetting is incomplete (45→37/150; Qwen3 41→32/150), not near zero. Stronger settings cost retain/GSM8K (Qwen3 η=1e-5), and at low strength forget rises 41→45 (r11,r14,r15,r13,r17,r29,r32,r33,r34,r35,r36,r41,r47).
relationships.display_finding: Target successes fell from 45 to 37 out of 150 and from 41 to 32 on Qwen3, while stronger settings damaged retention/GSM8K and weak settings increased Qwen3 target successes from 41 to 45.
